inspection_scope: Complete data-only review of the script, rhetorical chapter, both setups, beat contracts, setup boundary, semantic centers, planned hierarchy, dominant actions, before/after states, environments, composition, and continuity lifecycle.

checks.evidence: In s2, the cost-tray rule is combined with the unrelated inspection lens, scanner cables, and stamping machinery. These remain large and active, forcing one physical world to communicate inspection and price measurement simultaneously.

The b2 before/after states explicitly retain active inspection machinery after inspection is no longer discussed. The stated persistence reason—retaining mechanisms because they were built—provides no current semantic meaning.

In s1, the lens/page inspection group conflicts with a receipt pile designated as the focal target and pricing/receipt depth cues. In s2, the cost group and obsolete inspection-machinery group occupy equal space and remain active.

The unrelated inspection and cost propositions retain subject framing, the same paper-backboard/work-surface environment, the same participant placement logic, the same materials, and much of the same machinery. The nominal hard cut does not create a materially distinct composition.

No continuity token is declared or justified, yet the entire inspection apparatus effectively crosses into s2. The lens, cables, and stamps obscure the new cost claim instead of one meaningful document or result carrying across the cut.
Pricing placards and receipts appear in s1 despite its inspection rule, while s2 explicitly includes obsolete lens, cables, and stamps with no current story or location purpose.
The structure announces a hard reset between inspection and cost, but b2 retains the prior set and active machinery. The semantic rule changes without a useful visual reset.

In s1, the planned center is the inspection lens and page, but the focal_target is the receipt pile. In s2, the tray competes with multiple large, opaque, animated inspection mechanisms occupying equal space.
The planned central actions themselves encode both propositions: a lens exposes a broken line, and receipt weight lowers a cost tray. Captions are not required to supply those basic meanings.

setup_assessments.evidence: The inspection action is visible, but its hierarchy and semantic boundary are compromised by a receipt-pile focal target and pricing/receipt set elements belonging to the later cost proposition.
The cost rule is visible, but obsolete inspection mechanisms remain large, active, opaque, and equally prominent, defeating the planned reset and competing with the tray.

violations.observation: The cost setup simultaneously operates a receipt-weight rule and several unrelated inspection rules.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Remove the lens, scanner cables, and stamps from s2; let the tray and receipts alone govern the cost setup.

violations.observation: Inspection mechanisms remain active after their claim is complete, without expressing price or another current meaning.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Clear the inspection apparatus at the boundary and begin s2 from an empty cost tray or a single justified carried document.

violations.observation: s1 combines an inspection center with a receipt/pricing focal group, while s2 gives the cost group and obsolete inspection group comparable prominence.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Confine s1 to the document, lens, and revealed break; confine s2 to the tray and one receipt/cost group.

violations.observation: Both unrelated propositions use the same subject-scale paper-workbench staging, participant logic, and materials, with the earlier machinery continuing into the second setup.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Make the hard cut real by staging s2 around a distinct dominant silhouette—such as an isolated scale/tray—and exclude the inspection-stage layout.

violations.observation: The undeclared continuity payload is effectively the whole inspection set rather than a meaningful token with a destination.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Carry only the inspected document if identity continuity is needed, record it as a continuity token, and retire every inspection mechanism at the cut.

violations.observation: Pricing and receipt elements in s1 anticipate an unrelated claim, and the lens, cables, and stamps in s2 have no current story, location, action, or balance function.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Remove future-cost dressing from s1 and obsolete inspection geometry from s2.

violations.observation: The declared hard-cut boundary does not reset the world when the semantic verb changes from inspect to measure cost.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: End s1 on the exposed break, then hard-cut to a cleared, cost-specific stage containing only the justified carried document and tray.

violations.observation: s1 names both the centered lens/page and receipt pile as focal targets; s2 explicitly gives animated obsolete machinery equal space with the tray.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Set the lens contact as s1's sole dominant region and the receipt-to-tray contact as s2's sole dominant region, removing equal-scale competing machinery.

limits: This data-only review can assess planned structure, hierarchy, semantics, and lifecycles, but cannot establish rendered legibility, actual mobile-glance performance, pixel visibility, motion execution, or listening experience.
